questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always loved the spanish culture and the city of Barcelona, and I have always wanted to try and live abroad, so this was the perfect opportunity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. Some things were very different to the school at home in Copenhagen, and for that reason it took some time to understand. The teachers also weren't always very good at answering the questions that students had, but the international students office were always helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The school was very late to communicate when we had to start the semester and where we had to meet, so I had some help from the international students office with answering some of my questions about this. Apart from that I didn't need much assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The school didn't give us much information and the info we received came very late.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The prices are pretty similar to Copenhagen. I used the website called spotahome. It worked fine for me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit expensive, but if you take your time it is possible to find something for a reasonable price.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. It took some time because of some technical issues, but overall it went quite well.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They needed to know my personal details and what courses I planned to take. I later had to register for the courses. I happens in a "first come, first served" kind of way, where they open for course registration at a certain time, and the people who apply first get the courses. I was ready when they opened the registration and was able to get the courses that I wanted, but I heard about other people who didn't get what they wanted, so I recommend that you are ready when it opens.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emailing with the international students office was very helpful, but it was all pretty simple, and I didn't need much help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready when they open for course registration!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was a bit lower than in Copenhagen, but I had to do five courses, so there were a bit more to keep track of than I was used to. But overall the academic programme was easier than I was used to.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Easier than in Copenhagen

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Copenhagen I was used to doing one exam at the end of the semester to decide my final grade, but at UB they did continuous assessment, meaning we had to do test and assignments during the semester, which all counted towards the final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economic history of the world, Game theory, Global Sustainability, International Economics, Cooperate Finance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economic history of the world and Game theory were very good courses

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Buying a few things that were needed for the apartment. Stuff such as a dryer and so on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was a bit cheaper than in Copenhagen, but still not super cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you want to get involved in different non-academic opportunities there are plenty of different opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not much. I mostly arranged social activities by myself.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of instagram groups for Erasmus students that arrange parties, trips and other stuff. That's a good and fun way to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go and explore the city. Find a local coffee shop and other nice places in your area. I would also recommend to arrange social activities with other exchange students in your off time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. The most difficult thing to adjust to was that the supermarkets were closed on Sundays.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to find out which other students from Copenhagen are going to UB as well before you leave. But also try to connect with people from other countries. To me this was easiest to do by speaking to people during class especially in the first weeks. Other people are just as interested in meeting new friends as you are, so don't hesitate to ask if they want to go out for a beer.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't know much Spanish so it was a bit difficult to speak with some of the locals. So try to learn as much spanish as possible before you go. However, the younger generation were generally good English speakers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are generally more open than in Denmark, so it is easy to connect with new people. I'm also a big fan of the football culture in the city as well as the food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be ready to apply when they open the course registration
2. Be open to meeting other students
3. Be patient with the school. Sometimes they can be very slow to communicate things.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new friends I made and the experience of living in another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to miss my, friends, family and girlfriend at times, but when I came home I was nice to feel that nothing had changed and that we were still just as good friends as before I left.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
